text:
You grade one workflow job of Rho-Bank's procedure library against an answer key. An answering
agent serves customers by following this job exactly, as it is shown below (its steps, conditions,
arguments, rules and the facts it asks for; the quotes behind them are not shown to the agent).
For each fact in the key, decide whether the job leads the agent to it; for each trap, decide
whether the job tells the agent to do it. Judge only what the job says, not what a good agent
would know without it.

Facts:
- right: a step, an argument or a rule leads the agent to the fact for every case the fact names.
- partly: it does for some of the cases the fact names and is silent on the others, or it says
  it so loosely that an agent following it could give another answer.
- missing: nothing in the job leads the agent to it; the agent would have to work it out alone.
- wrong: the job leads the agent to a different answer for at least one case the fact names, even
  if it is right for others.

Traps:
- present: a step, an argument or a rule tells the agent to do it, for some case.
- absent: nothing in the job does.

Then list the conflicts: two steps, arguments or rules that give the same case different
instructions, so an agent could follow either.

Job: pin_lock_investigation_protocol

For each card that cannot be unlocked, the successful transactions from its earliest declined attempt to now were reviewed, the customer was told whether money was taken, and whatever the customer accepted (dispute, closure and replacement, PIN reset or transfer) was carried out. A security-hold card got the transfer offer, and the customer's choice was respected.",

  {

   "by": "model",
   "do": "For each locked card, check the automatic triggers first:\n- A security_hold card cannot be unlocked by chat agents; offer the security-team transfer (check_security_hold).\n- If several cards are locked, investigate every card before unlocking any of them.\n- If a card on the account was replaced as stolen in the last 90 days, enhanced verification is required (check_recent_stolen).",

   "id": "check_security_hold",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "For each locked card, read pin_lock_reason. If it is 'security_hold', do not score or unlock the card. Offer to transfer the customer to the security team for that card, and keep handling their other cards normally.",
   "call": null,

   "lookup": [

   "after": [

  },
  {
   "id": "check_recent_stolen",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If any card on the account has issue_reason 'stolen' with date_issued within 90 days of get_current_time, enhanced verification is required. No tool performs enhanced verification, so do not unlock the card. Follow the Step 6 path instead: check_unauthorized, then cannot_unlock_options.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards",
    "time"
   ],
   "after": [
    "triggers"
   ],
   "if": "a card on the account has issue_reason 'stolen' and date_issued within 90 days"
  },
  {
   "id": "score",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "Score each locked card that has no security hold and is on an account with no card replaced as stolen in the last 90 days, using the flags below. Never reveal the calculation.\n- A1: compare the declined city with the address city. Same city 0; other city, same state 1; other state 2; other country 3.\n- A2: 2 locations 1; 3+ locations 2.\n- A3: all successful transactions in the last 7 days at home, but declines elsewhere: +1.\n- B1: hour of the attempt. 6AM-10PM 0; 10PM-12AM 1; 12-2AM 2; 2-6AM 3.\n- B2: last successful PIN use 7-30 days ago 1; over 30 days 2.\n- B3: gap between attempts. 2-5 min 1; 1-2 min 2; under 1 min 3.\n- C1: decreasing amounts 2.\n- C2: all round hundreds 1.\n- C3: 2-5x the average ATM withdrawal 1; over 5x 2.\n- C4: 80-100% of daily_atm_limit 1; attempts totalling over the limit 2.\n- D1: 1, 2 or 3+ prior locks in 90 days score 1, 2 or 3.\n- D2: card age 1-3 months 1; under 1 month 2.\n- D3: another card with a velocity block +1; with a fraud alert +2.\n- E1: account age 3-6 months 1; under 3 months 2.\n- E2: 1 overdraft 1; 2+ overdrafts 2.\n- E3: balance $50-100 1; under $50 2.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards",
    "txns",
    "accounts",
    "identify",
    "time"
   ],
   "after": [
    "triggers",
    "check_security_hold",
    "check_other_locked",
    "check_recent_stolen"

  },
  {
   "id": "ask_location",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the card's score is 5 or higher and the Location Mismatch flag (A1) scored, ask: 'I see your card was locked after failed PIN attempts at [location]. Were you at that location?'\n- Yes: remove the location flags and rescore.\n- No: keep the score and proceed with caution. The card's outcome then follows decide.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "score",
    "txns"
   ],
   "after": [
    "score"
   ],
   "if": "the card's score is 5 or higher and the Location Mismatch flag (A1) scored"
  },
  {
   "id": "ask_time",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the card's score is 5 or higher and the time-of-day flag scored 2 or more, ask: 'These attempts occurred at [time]. Were you trying to use your card at that time?'\n- If the customer confirms, remove the time flag and recalculate.\n- If they say they were asleep or similar, the card is CRITICAL (likely fraud).\nDo not ask this for a card scoring below 5.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "score",
    "txns"
   ],
   "after": [
    "score"
   ],
   "if": "the card's score is 5 or higher and the time-of-day flag (B1) is 2 or more"
  },
  {
   "id": "ask_amount",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the card's score is 5 or higher and the amount-pattern flag (C1) scored, ask: 'The attempts were for [amount 1], then [amount 2], then [amount 3]. Do you remember trying those specific amounts?'\n- If they confirm, remove the amount-pattern flag and recalculate.\n- If they deny it or seem confused, keep the flag.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "score",
    "txns"
   ],
   "after": [
    "score"
   ],
   "if": "the card's score is 5 or higher and the amount pattern flag scored"
  },
  {
   "id": "velocity_flag_stays",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "B3 scores 3 when consecutive failed attempts are less than 1 minute apart. The Step 4 questions cover only the location, amount-pattern and time-of-day flags, so the customer's answers never remove B3. That holds even when the customer says the attempts were theirs. The card therefore keeps a 3-point flag, and single_flag_escalation applies.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "score",
    "txns"
   ],
   "after": [
    "score"
   ],
   "if": "the card's consecutive failed attempts were less than 1 minute apart (B3 = 3)"

  {
   "id": "medium_question",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "For a final score of 5-7, ask: 'I see failed PIN attempts on your card. Were those attempts yours?' Unlock only if the customer says yes. If they say no, follow cannot_unlock_options.",
   "call": null,

   "lookup": [
    "score",
    "ask_location",
    "ask_amount"

   "after": [
    "ask_location",
    "ask_time",

   "id": "decide",

Do not unlock. Run check_unauthorized, then recommend card closure and replacement through cannot_unlock_options.\n- 3+ prior locks: reset the PIN instead of unlocking.",

    "ask_location",
    "ask_time",

    "medium_question"

    "ask_time",
    "ask_amount",
    "medium_question"

   "lookup": [
    "cards",
    "score",
    "decide"

   "after": [
    "decide"

No tool performs supervisor review, so follow check_unauthorized and cannot_unlock_options; those include the security-team transfer. For D1 at 3+ prior locks, the PIN reset in three_plus_locks_reset is required as well.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "score",
    "ask_time",
    "ask_location"
   ],
   "after": [
    "decide"
   ],
   "if": "any single flag equals 3 points"
  },
  {
   "id": "very_high_branch",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "For a final score of 11-14, tell the customer the card cannot be unlocked on this call. No callback or enhanced-verification tool is documented, so offer the cannot_unlock_options.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "decide"
   ],
   "after": [
    "decide"
   ],
   "if": "the card's final score is 11-14"
  },
  {

## The answer key

- K1 (overnight_denial): declined attempts in another US state between 2 AM and 6 AM that the customer denies, saying she was asleep at home, make the card CRITICAL (likely fraud): it is not unlocked, whatever the total; the job reaches this for a different state, not only for a different country
- K2 (critical_outcome): a CRITICAL card with no successful unauthorized transaction is recommended for closure and replacement because fraud is suspected, and on the customer's yes it is closed and a replacement ordered for the same checking account (the closing and the order may run in the jobs this one names)
- K3 (suspicious_period): the suspicious period checked for successful unauthorized transactions is the window of the declined attempts the customer denies (from the first of them to now): successful transactions before it, her usual home-city activity, are not put to her as possibly unauthorized and not disputed, so a card whose period holds only declined attempts gets no dispute and she is told no money was taken
- K4 (admitted_attempts): a card whose declined attempts the customer confirms were hers (at that store, at that time, for that amount: she mixed up PINs) has its location flags removed and its score recalculated, and with no 3-point flag, fewer than 3 prior locks and a recalculated score of 10 or less it is cleared for unlock: not closed, not escalated, not sent to the cannot-unlock options
- K5 (card_order): locked cards on different checking accounts are taken one at a time, in the order the customer chooses, each to its outcome before the next is investigated; the trigger to finish investigating every locked card before any unlock applies only to locked cards on the same checking account
- K6 (two_prior_locks): a card cleared for unlock with 2 prior PIN locks in the last 90 days must be asked 'This is your third PIN lock in 90 days. Would you like me to reset your PIN to a new number?', and on a yes its PIN is reset to the new PIN the customer chooses (reset_debit_card_pin_6284, here or in the PIN-reset job this one names)
- K7 (security_hold): a card with pin_lock_reason security_hold is not scored, unlocked or reset: the agent offers a transfer to the security team, and when the customer declines it does nothing more on that card (no transfer, no write)

## The traps

- T1: every locked card the customer has, on any checking account, is investigated and scored before any of them is unlocked (the same-account trigger applied across accounts)
- T2: a PIN reset is offered, beside closure and a transfer, for a CRITICAL card (one whose overnight attempts the customer slept through); the reset clears the lock, so taking it unlocks a card that cannot be unlocked
- T4: the suspicious period reaches back before the first declined attempt the customer denies (to the last transaction she confirms as hers, or over the recent successful activity), so earlier home-city transactions she does not recognise are put to her and disputed
